# C06 baseline B: catalogue-derived references

Four references can help with configurable pod process-namespace sharing. These are proposed transfers from documented mechanisms, not claims of deployment or demonstrated usefulness for this design.

1. **Docker's explicit PID-namespace mode** — [primary documentation](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/). Docker defaults to isolated PID namespaces and provides `--pid=container:<name|id>` to join another container's namespace. This supplies a concrete opt-in mechanism while preserving the separate-namespace behavior expected by legacy images. Its interface is per container, so a pod implementation would need to derive every member's setting from one pod-level choice. **Date: unknown; live documentation.**

2. **OCI Linux namespace configuration** — [primary specification](https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/blob/main/config-linux.md). A `pid` entry with a namespace path joins that namespace; an entry without a path creates one. This can implement one shared namespace across a pod. Omitting the namespace type instead inherits the runtime namespace, so that omission must not be mistaken for requesting a private namespace. **Date: unknown; live main branch.**

3. **rkt's pod execution stage** — [primary architecture documentation](https://github.com/rkt/rkt/blob/master/Documentation/devel/architecture.md). Its systemd/nspawn stage launches a pod-level PID 1 and then the applications, providing a concrete example of pod-scoped namespace ownership and lifecycle. This is useful as an architectural reference, but application processes no longer occupy PID 1; copying that behavior unconditionally would violate the legacy-image requirement. Importing its general-purpose supervisor is outside the requested scope. **Date: unknown; archived master branch without a verified historical revision.**

4. **nsenter's existing-namespace entry mechanism** — [primary manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/nsenter.1.html). Its target-PID and fork behavior provides an executable reference for starting a process in an existing PID namespace. The linked [PID namespace manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/pid_namespaces.7.html) supplies useful constraints: membership is fixed at creation, PID 1's exit terminates namespace members, and procfs visibility depends on the mounting namespace. These support implementation and compatibility checks, but do not provide a pod API. **Date: post-decision; the consulted manual versions are dated 2026-05-24 and 2026-05-13.**

**Design translation, as an inference:** preserve the existing separate-namespace behavior by default and make sharing an explicit pod-wide option. In shared mode, give every participating container the same namespace target, establish its lifetime before launching applications, and document the loss of application PID 1 behavior. Apply the decision when processes are created. Keep multiple sharing groups, per-container policy, and a general-purpose init system outside this design.

Discovery came from the opened [Awesome Linux Containers](https://github.com/Friz-zy/awesome-linux-containers) and its linked [Awesome Docker](https://github.com/veggiemonk/awesome-docker) catalogues. Every candidate has an opened primary verification source. No pre-cutoff version was verified: unknown dates must not be interpreted as evidence of availability by 2018-01-24. One rkt documentation-directory fetch failed; its linked architecture page was accessible.

This is translation by an internal separate-context GPT-6 Astra Pro agent, not a human study or a different-model comparison. The run used three exact catalogue-restricted search queries and 24 conservatively counted page operations, including six in-page finds, repeated reads, and one failed fetch. No specific target-proposal exposure was recognized; model-memory leakage is not controlled.
